text: {"overall_winner": "A", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Directly quotes and cites the article with paragraph numbers for each supporting point, e.g., \"None of the cars developed so far are completely driverless\" (7)", "quality": "Textual grounding", "description": "The essay anchors each claim in specific quoted evidence from the source article, giving it credibility and precision."}, {"evidence": "Each body paragraph develops one distinct argument (not fully driverless; safety/liability concerns) with explanation of why each is a problem", "quality": "Focused argument development", "description": "The essay sustains a clear line of reasoning within each paragraph, explaining the implications of each point rather than merely listing them."}, {"evidence": "Consistently maintains the position that driverless cars are not beneficial and returns to this thesis in the introduction, body, and conclusion", "quality": "Coherent thesis control", "description": "The essay keeps a single, consistent position threaded throughout, with each section reinforcing the central claim."}, {"evidence": "Explores the liability question of who is at fault in an accident, connecting it to traffic laws and safety", "quality": "Nuanced causal reasoning", "description": "The essay examines the downstream consequences and unresolved questions raised by the technology rather than only restating surface benefits or drawbacks."}, {"evidence": "Uses precise connective language such as \"This is negative because,\" \"The reason for this is because,\" and \"which shows how\" to link evidence to claims", "quality": "Explicit reasoning links", "description": "The essay makes the logical relationship between evidence and conclusion explicit, guiding the reader through the argument."}]}
